paperclip.usage: Direct full-text virtual-filesystem reads with line-pinned citations; no repository clone.

sources.title: Boosting the Sliding Frank-Wolfe solver for 3D deconvolution
sources.used_claim: The displayed SFW algorithm computes a certificate maximum, augments support, adjusts weights only, performs joint local descent over weights and positions, and removes zero-weight masses. This exact operator order motivated the native C2 implementation.
sources.scope_limit: The paper treats continuous sparse deconvolution, not the nonconvex C2 max-ratio.

sources.title: The Sliding Frank-Wolfe Algorithm and its Application to Super-Resolution Microscopy
sources.used_claim: The original method interleaves convex atom addition with nonconvex movement of existing spikes and proves finite termination under problem-specific hypotheses.
sources.scope_limit: Its theorem is for BLASSO sparse inverse problems and is not used as a convergence guarantee for C2.

sources.title: Sparse Inverse Problems Over Measures: Equivalence of the Conditional Gradient and Exchange Methods
sources.used_claim: Conditional-gradient and exchange views support a finite support-insertion plus fully corrective re-optimization vocabulary.
sources.scope_limit: The equivalence and convergence results concern a convex program over nonnegative measures, not C2.

sources.title: The second autocorrelation inequality: towards a constructive proof that C >= 0.901564
sources.used_claim: Primary C2 work uses direct gradient optimization and 23-to-115-to-575 continuation, supporting native-objective rather than proxy-only evaluation.

exa.usage: Deep publication search and primary-source inspection; the configured credential was read from Keychain and was not copied into any artifact.

requests.purpose: Find primary support-insertion, fully corrective, joint support-relocation, and pruning algorithms over measures.

sources.title: The Sliding Frank-Wolfe Algorithm and its Application to Super-Resolution Microscopy
sources.used_claim: Certificate-guided spike insertion is interleaved with nonconvex movement of all spikes.
sources.scope_limit: Only the operator pattern transfers as a heuristic.

sources.title: Boosting the Sliding Frank-Wolfe solver for 3D deconvolution
sources.used_claim: The primary algorithm presentation makes the support augmentation, weights-only correction, joint position/weight descent, and zero-mass pruning sequence explicit.
sources.scope_limit: Its deconvolution objective and assumptions differ from C2.

sources.title: Sparse Inverse Problems Over Measures: Equivalence of the Conditional Gradient and Exchange Methods
sources.used_claim: Exchange and conditional-gradient methods give a primary-source framework for support insertion and fully corrective finite subproblems.
sources.scope_limit: No theorem from the convex measure problem is asserted for C2.

arena_corpus.usage: Audited before the run to avoid duplicating already exhausted C2 directions.

methodological_conclusion: Primary sources justify testing certificate-guided insertion followed by fully corrective amplitude and support relocation as a global mechanism. They do not predict success for the nonsmooth nonconvex C2 ratio. The exact bounded implementation produced a negative frontier, so the result applies only to the tested finite atom family and relocation grid.
